title: Fitting by Balance
subtitle: how the dial and the sliders find their places
name: ModelInMotion_LogisticFE_E06_FittingByBalance
status: DRAFT: script under review together with its animatic.

segments.visual: The log-odds panel. The dial and sliders drift from an unfitted position and settle; the lines settle with them.

sentences.text: For two episodes, the dial and the sliders have simply known where to stop.
Four sliders settled, the dial settled, and we read off the answers.

segments.visual: Beside the panel: 103 patients, and who came back.

sentences.text: But nobody handed them those answers. All they had was the data: 103 patients, and who came back.
sentences.say: But nobody handed them those answers. All they had was the data: one hundred and three patients, and who came back.

segments.visual: The question, in two lines.

sentences.text: So what makes one setting of the dial and sliders better than another?
And how do they find the best one?

segments.visual: Series logo and wordmark; arc and episode title.

sentences.text: Welcome back to Model in Motion.
Today: fitting by balance.

segments.visual: All 103 patients as chips in five trays. A label: the plain guess, 41% for everyone.

sentences.text: Start with any setting at all. Here is the plainest: every patient, at every clinic, gets the overall rate, 41%.
sentences.say: Start with any setting at all. Here is the plainest: every patient, at every clinic, gets the overall rate, forty-one percent.

segments.visual: Two example chips: a filled one marked 41%, an empty one marked 59%.

sentences.text: Now ask of each patient: what probability did this guess give to what actually happened?
For a patient who was readmitted, 41%. For one who wasn't, 59%.
sentences.say: For a patient who was readmitted, forty-one percent. For one who wasn't, fifty-nine percent.

segments.visual: The product: 0.41 to the power 42 times 0.59 to the power 61, about 6 × 10⁻³¹. Then its logarithm: −69.6.

sentences.text: Multiply those 103 numbers together, and you have the probability the guess gave to the whole story. That is its likelihood.
sentences.say: Multiply those one hundred and three numbers together, and you have the probability the guess gave to the whole story. That is its likelihood.

sentences.text: It is tiny: a decimal point followed by thirty zeros. So we take its logarithm instead: minus 69.6.
sentences.say: It is tiny: a decimal point followed by thirty zeros. So we take its logarithm instead: minus sixty-nine point six.

segments.visual: A height bar, with its level at −69.63 near the bottom and an arrow pointing up.

sentences.text: Think of that number as a height. A better guess stands higher.
The height itself means nothing. Only the climb from one guess to another does.

segments.visual: The machine: a slider and an observed-minus-expected meter for each clinic, the dial with its own meter, and the height bar. All set to the plain guess.

sentences.text: So which way is up? Bring back the meter from Episode 3: observed on one side, expected on the other.
sentences.say: So which way is up? Bring back the meter from Episode three: observed on one side, expected on the other.

sentences.text: Here is one for every clinic, under the plain guess.

segments.visual: Dune's, Birch's and Elm's meters are picked out in turn: +2.11, +1.77, −4.49.

sentences.text: Dune expected 4.9 readmissions and saw 7. Birch expected 12.2 and saw 14. Elm expected 4.5 and saw none.
sentences.say: Dune expected four point nine readmissions and saw seven. Birch expected twelve point two and saw fourteen. Elm expected four point five and saw none.

segments.visual: An arrow beside each slider: up where observed is above expected, down where it is below. Caption: tilt = slope.

sentences.text: And here is the fact that makes fitting possible.
Each meter's tilt is exactly the slope of the height in that clinic's gamma.
Observed above expected: push the slider up. Observed below: pull it down.

segments.visual: Dune's slider rises. Of the clinic meters only Dune's moves; its expected count climbs to 7.0 and the height bar rises by 0.75. The dial's meter eases from +10.24 to +9.19.

sentences.text: Try it with Dune. Push its slider up, and among the clinics, only Dune's meter responds.
Its expected count climbs toward 7, and the height rises with it.
sentences.say: Its expected count climbs toward seven, and the height rises with it.

segments.visual: Dune's meter is level. Then the slider is pushed further: the meter tips the other way and the height bar drops. It returns to level.

sentences.text: When the meter is level, the height is as high as this one slider can take it.
Push further, and the meter tips the other way. The height falls.

segments.visual: Back at the plain guess. The dial's yellow meter is picked out: 29 observed, 18.8 expected.

sentences.text: The dial has a meter too. It weighs only the higher-risk patients: 29 of them were readmitted, and the plain guess expected fewer than 19.
sentences.say: The dial has a meter too. It weighs only the higher-risk patients: twenty-nine of them were readmitted, and the plain guess expected fewer than nineteen.

segments.visual: The dial turns to 0.91 and its meter levels. Four clinic meters shift as it turns; Elm's does not.

sentences.text: Turn the dial up until that meter is level.
But look at the clinics. Every one that has higher-risk patients has shifted.

segments.visual: Caption: nothing settles one piece at a time.

sentences.text: So nothing can be settled one piece at a time. The dial and the sliders have to find their places together.

segments.visual: Dial and sliders move together to the fit. Four clinic meters and the dial's meter come level; the height bar climbs.

sentences.text: And here is where they stop. The dial at 2.02, and the sliders where we found them two episodes ago.
sentences.say: And here is where they stop. The dial at two point zero two, and the sliders where we found them two episodes ago.

sentences.text: Four clinic meters are level, and so is the dial's.

segments.visual: The four expected counts are picked out: 13.0, 14.0, 8.0, 7.0.

sentences.text: In each of those four clinics, expected now equals observed: 13, 14, 8 and 7.
sentences.say: In each of those four clinics, expected now equals observed: thirteen, fourteen, eight and seven.

sentences.text: That is what fitting is: balancing.

segments.visual: A note under Alder: 8.2 + 4.8 expected, 8 + 5 observed.

sentences.text: One detail. The balance holds for each clinic's total, not for each group inside it.
Alder expected 8.2 among its lower-risk patients and 4.8 among its higher-risk ones. Not 8 and 5. But together, 13.
sentences.say: Alder expected eight point two among its lower-risk patients and four point eight among its higher-risk ones. Not eight and five. But together, thirteen.

segments.visual: Elm's slider keeps sliding down, past the end of its track. Its meter approaches level and never reaches it; the height bar creeps up.

sentences.text: And Elm? Its meter can never level. With no readmissions, expected stays above observed wherever the slider sits.
So the slider keeps sliding, gaining a little less height each time. We'll come back to Elm.

segments.visual: Beside the height bar: −69.6 to −55.6.

sentences.text: With Elm's slider run all the way down, the height has climbed from minus 69.6 to minus 55.6.
sentences.say: With Elm's slider run all the way down, the height has climbed from minus sixty-nine point six to minus fifty-five point six.

segments.visual: A chart: dial position along the bottom, height up the side. A dot traces the curve from left to right.

sentences.text: One last picture. For each position of the dial, level the clinics' meters, and record the height.

segments.visual: The top is marked at 2.02. A second mark at 1.75, the pooled step, sits just below it on the left.

sentences.text: The result is a hill, with one top, at 2.02.
sentences.say: The result is a hill, with one top, at two point zero two.

sentences.text: The pooled step from Episode 3, 1.75, sits a little way down the left side.
sentences.say: The pooled step from Episode three, one point seven five, sits a little way down the left side.

segments.visual: A bracket over the rounded top.

sentences.text: And notice how gently the top is rounded. That gentleness is the roughness we keep promising to measure.

segments.visual: Three recap cards, each with a small icon.

sentences.text: Let's gather it up.
A guess is scored by the probability it gave to what actually happened.
Each clinic's meter, observed minus expected, says which way its slider should move.
And at the best fit, every meter that can level is level.

segments.visual: A caution card: level meters do not show the model is right.

sentences.text: A caution. Level meters do not show that the model is right.
Any model with a number for each clinic will level them. Whether it is right has to be judged inside the clinics, and that comes later.

segments.visual: The hill again, small, with a climber's path sketched toward the top; the next episode's title.

sentences.text: We have seen where the top of the hill is, not how to get there. No formula gives it.
Next time: climbing the hill.

segments.visual: Series end card with the next episode title.

sentences.text: This has been Model in Motion. Thanks for following the story.
